result.title: Do Artificial Neural Networks Need Dendritic Nanotubes? Two Reasons for Shrinking Importance Estimates in Continual Learning
result.comment: Github: https://github.com/Saurav-K-Aryal/Do-Artificial-Neural-Networks-Need-Dendritic-Nanotubes-.git 21 pages, 3 figures, 10 tables. Simulation and figure scripts are included as ancillary files
result.summary: Regularization-based continual learning protects each parameter in proportion to an estimate of its importance, yet these estimates come from finite samples and heuristics and are used as if they were exact. We report four studies that start from a biologically inspired mechanism and end with a statistical explanation of it. Motivated by dendritic nanotubes, we let transient lateral links diffuse importance tags between hidden units. Links between co-active units gave no significant gain, but random links with lifetimes of 25 or 200 steps raised final accuracy on 20-task Permuted MNIST by 1.5 to 2.6 points. We show that random diffusion implements linear shrinkage of importance toward the layer mean in expectation. A simulation of the link process alone predicts shrinkage weights of 0.23 and 0.52 for these lifetimes, and graph-free shrinkage at 0.25 and 0.5 reproduces both the accuracy and the dispersion of the consolidated importance, while every activity-dependent rule did worse than random links. A five-seed screen across EWC, SI, and MAS found nominal gains for SI and MAS on Permuted MNIST and losses on task-incremental Split CIFAR-100, where forgetting was small and shrinkage cost plasticity. Varying the number of importance samples then separates two mechanisms on Permuted MNIST. For EWC, the gain fell by about ten points per tenfold increase in samples, from 19.6 points with 10 samples to -0.4 with 1000, a variance effect. For MAS, a gain of about one point persisted at 1000 samples, consistent with a bias in the importance measure rather than noise. Shrinkage had no detectable effect for MAS on a domain-incremental CIFAR-100 benchmark. Finally, we show that a standard heteroscedastic empirical Bayes rule shrinks the largest Fisher-type estimates most, which may explain its poor results, and point to a log-scale alternative.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究持续学习中基于正则化的参数重要性估计：受树突纳米管启发用随机横向连接扩散重要性标签，证明其等价于向层均值做线性收缩，并通过 EWC（样本量导致的方差效应）、SI、MAS（重要性度量的偏差）多组实验解释增益与失效条件。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于有限样本重要性估计的收缩、方差与偏差分离分析，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态或视觉 token 的贡献分配与训练监督提供借备案线索，但原论文不涉及多模态推理，迁移可行性待核查。
